title: Average-case optimality of standard Shellsort
formal: Is there a deterministic increment sequence depending only on \(n\) for which standard Shellsort uses \(O(n\log n)\) expected comparisons on a uniformly random permutation of \(n\) keys?

import_provenance.original_statement: Is there a fixed, n-dependent increment sequence for standard Shellsort whose expected number of comparisons is O(n log n) on a uniformly random input permutation? Here each increment means fully insertion-sorting the corresponding residue-class subsequences.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Goodrich's randomized Shellsort and later Zig-zag Sort already attain O(n log n) for different procedures; they do not settle this standard-Shellsort question. The selection is a historical open problem connected to his work, not an assertion of current activity.
